title: Power Automate flow: machine downtime report from Forms to Planner task and Teams alert
summary: Step-by-step cloud flow that turns a Microsoft Forms downtime report into a SharePoint log row, a Planner task for the right trade and a Teams alert, with a shorter deadline for safety-relevant stops.
body:
Purpose: operators report a machine stop in 30 seconds from a phone or a shopfloor terminal, and the right maintenance trade sees it as a task with a deadline, while the cell lead sees an alert in Teams. The flow also writes a log row, so the stop appears in your downtime Pareto later. It does not stop a machine and it is not a safety system. A person standing at the machine decides what is safe.

=== Prerequisites ===
- A Microsoft Forms form (example questions below), a SharePoint list 'Downtime Log', a Planner plan (basic plan; the Planner connector supports basic plans only, per the connector page) with one bucket per trade, and a Teams channel such as 'Maintenance Alerts'.
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.
- Own the flow in a solution with a service account or a dedicated flow owner, not on a personal account of one maintenance planner. If that person leaves, the flow stops.

=== Data model (example) ===
Form 'Report a machine stop': Machine (choice list of machine IDs), Reason group (choice: Mechanical, Electrical, Tooling, Material shortage, Quality hold, Other), Safety-relevant? (choice Yes or No), What happened (long text).
List 'Downtime Log': Title (text), Machine (text), ReasonGroup (choice), SafetyRelevant (Yes/No), Description (multiple lines), ReportedAt (date and time), ReportedBy (text), PlannerTaskId (text), Status (choice: Open, Closed). Create ReportedBy as text; whether a name is stored at all is a decision for your works council (see the privacy section).

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: Microsoft Forms, 'When a new response is submitted' (operation CreateFormWebhook). Pick the form in Form Id.
1. Microsoft Forms, 'Get response details' (GetFormResponseById). Form Id: the same form. Response Id: use the dynamic content 'List of response notifications Response Id'. The raw path is triggerOutputs()?['body/resourceData/responseId'] (check in your run history, the picker is safer than typing it). The trigger only tells you that a response exists; this action fetches the answers.
2. Compose actions, one per answer, so later expressions stay readable. Name them Machine, Reason, Safety and Description and fill each with the matching dynamic content of step 1. The internal question keys look like r followed by random characters, which is why you pick them from the list instead of typing them.
3. Compose 'LocalNow': convertTimeZone(utcNow(), 'UTC', 'W. Europe Standard Time', 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm'). Replace the Windows time zone name with the one for your plant. The Teams message and the log show local time; the flow itself works in UTC.
4. Compose 'TradeOwner': if(equals(outputs('Reason'), 'Electrical'), 'maint-electrical@contoso.example', 'maint-mechanical@contoso.example'). For more than two trades use a Switch action on Reason instead of nested ifs. Use a shared mailbox or group address that still exists when people change roles.
5. SharePoint, 'Create item' (PostItem) in 'Downtime Log'. Title: concat(outputs('Machine'), ' - ', outputs('Reason')). Set Status to Open and ReportedAt to utcNow(). Keep the item output; its 'ID' and 'Link to item' are used below.
6. Planner, 'Create a task' (operation CreateTask_V3). Group Id and Plan Id from the pickers, Bucket Id from the trade, Title: concat('Stop ', outputs('Machine'), ': ', outputs('Reason')). Assigned User Ids: outputs('TradeOwner') (the connector takes user IDs or email addresses separated by semicolons). Due Date Time: if(equals(outputs('Safety'), 'Yes'), addHours(utcNow(), 2), addDays(utcNow(), 1)). The base action has no priority field. The 'Create a task (Preview)' action adds one (0 to 10, lower is more urgent; 1 urgent, 3 important, 5 medium, 9 low according to the connector page); use it only if your tenant accepts a preview action in production.
7. SharePoint, 'Update item' (operation PatchItem). Id: the ID from step 5. Write PlannerTaskId with outputs('Create_a_task')?['body/id'].
8. Condition on Safety equal to 'Yes'. If yes: Teams, 'Post message in a chat or channel' (PostMessageToConversation), Post as Flow bot, Post in Channel, to the maintenance channel and a second post to the safety officer channel. Text: 'SAFETY-RELEVANT STOP at [machine] reported [local time]. Task due in 2 hours.' plus the link to the item. If no: one normal post to the maintenance channel only.
Teams limits from the connector page: a message is limited to about 28 KB including HTML, posting to private channels is not supported, and cards need the Workflows app allowed in the Teams admin center.

=== Error handling ===
Put steps 5 to 8 in a Scope called Try. Add a second Scope called Catch with 'Configure run after' set to 'has failed' and 'has timed out' for Try. In Catch, send an email with Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email (V2)' to the flow owner group with the run link: concat('https://make.powerautomate.com/environments/', workflow()?['tags']?['environmentName'], '/flows/', workflow()?['name'], '/runs/', workflow()?['run']?['name']). Then add a Teams post to the channel: 'Automatic task creation failed, call maintenance directly'. The operator's report must never disappear silently; the Forms response itself remains stored, so you can replay it by resubmitting the trigger from run history.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Operator submits at 09:40 local (08:40 UTC in November, UTC+1): Machine CNC-07, Reason group Electrical, Safety-relevant Yes, text 'Spindle drive fault, smell of burning'. TradeOwner becomes maint-electrical@contoso.example. Due Date Time is addHours(utcNow(), 2), so 10:40 UTC, shown as 11:40 local. The log row, the Planner task and two Teams posts exist within a minute or two. The same report with Safety No and reason Material shortage would go to the mechanical owner with addDays(utcNow(), 1) as due date and one Teams post.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Treating the trigger output as the answers. Without step 1 you only have a response ID.
- Typing question keys by hand. Rename a question in Forms and the key can change; dynamic content picks up the new one after you re-pick it.
- Anonymous or external respondents. When the form does not record names, the responder fields are empty; do not build assignment on them.
- Assigning with a display name. The Planner 'Assigned User Ids' field needs an ID or email.
- Using a personal connection. Teams posts then appear 'from' that person; use Post as Flow bot, or a service account.
- Forgetting the time zone. utcNow() is UTC; a 'due today' task created at 23:30 local can be due 'tomorrow' in UTC terms.

=== Adapt it ===
Replace machines, reasons and trades. Add a second branch for Reason 'Quality hold' that starts your NCR flow. If you collect photos, Forms stores uploads in OneDrive or SharePoint and the answer arrives as a JSON string with file references (check the exact format in a test run); parse it with 'Parse JSON' and put the link into the task description rather than copying files.

=== Privacy and safety ===
Downtime reports can reveal who was at the machine. Ask your data protection officer and works council before storing ReportedBy, and agree who may read the log. Restrict the SharePoint list to maintenance, quality and the cell leads. Never put access codes, customer drawings or part serial numbers of controlled items in a Teams post if the channel has guests.

title: Power Automate flow: nonconformance report approval with severity routing and audit history
summary: Cloud flow for a SharePoint NCR register that routes approvals by severity (Minor, Major, Critical), writes decisions and comments back, and appends every step to a history list for audits.
body:
Purpose: a nonconformance report (NCR) is raised in a SharePoint list. The flow sends the proposed disposition for approval according to severity, records who decided what and when, informs the person who raised it, and keeps an append-only history. This supports your quality system; it does not replace it. Who may approve which disposition (rework, repair, use-as-is, scrap, return to supplier) is defined by your own procedures and, in aerospace, often by customer or design authority rules. The flow must reflect those rules, not invent them. Check them before you build.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'NCR Register' with versioning turned on, and a second list 'NCR History'.
- The Approvals connector stores approvals in Dataverse; in a non-default environment the database is provisioned when the connector is first used, and the first user must be an environment admin (Power Automate approvals documentation, read 20 Nov 2026).
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.
- A group or shared address for the quality manager role, so approvals are not stuck on one person's holiday.

=== Data model (example) ===
'NCR Register': Title (text, the NCR number), PartNumber (text), Severity (choice: Minor, Major, Critical), Description (multiple lines), ProposedDisposition (choice: Rework, Repair, Use as is, Scrap, Return to supplier), QualityEngineer (person), RaisedBy (person, default Created By), Status (choice: New, In approval, Approved, Rejected, Timed out), DecisionSummary (multiple lines), DecidedAt (date and time).
'NCR History': Title (NCR number), Step (text), Actor (text), Outcome (text), Comment (multiple lines), At (date and time). Give only the flow account write permission to this list; everybody else gets read at most.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: SharePoint 'When an item is created' on 'NCR Register'.
1. 'Update item': Status to 'In approval'. To avoid a loop, use this flow only on creation (not on 'modified').
2. 'Create item' in 'NCR History': Step 'Submitted', Actor from RaisedBy display name, At utcNow().
3. Switch on triggerOutputs()?['body/Severity/Value'] (choice columns return the label under /Value).
 Case Minor: Approvals, 'Start and wait for an approval' (StartAndWaitForAnApproval), Approval type 'Approve/Reject - First to respond', Assigned to the QualityEngineer email: triggerOutputs()?['body/QualityEngineer/Email'].
 Case Major: same action, type 'Approve/Reject - Everyone must approve', Assigned to the quality engineer and the production manager, separated by a semicolon.
 Case Critical: first approval of the quality engineer as above; if outcome is Approve, a second approval of the quality manager. Chain two actions instead of the 'Sequential approval' type when you want each step visible in the history.
 Title: concat('NCR ', triggerOutputs()?['body/Title'], ' - ', triggerOutputs()?['body/Severity/Value']). Details: Markdown text with part number, description and proposed disposition. Item link: the link to the item, so the approver opens the record.
 Settings: set the action timeout to P2D (ISO 8601, two days; check that the Settings pane of the approval action offers Timeout in your tenant).
4. After the approval, a Compose 'Outcome' that merges branches with coalesce: coalesce(body('Approval_critical_2')?['outcome'], body('Approval_critical_1')?['outcome'], body('Approval_major')?['outcome'], body('Approval_minor')?['outcome']). Skipped branches return null, which coalesce ignores. Valid responses for the basic types are 'Approve' and 'Reject' and they are case sensitive (connector page).
5. Select 'Comments': From coalesce(body('Approval_critical_2')?['responses'], body('Approval_critical_1')?['responses'], body('Approval_major')?['responses'], body('Approval_minor')?['responses']), map concat(item()?['responder']?['displayName'], ': ', item()?['comments']). The responses array holds one entry per approver; check the field names in a test run. Then join(body('Comments'), ' | ') gives one text for the register. Approval timestamps are UTC.
6. Condition equals(outputs('Outcome'), 'Approve'): Yes updates Status to Approved, No to Rejected. Write DecisionSummary and DecidedAt: utcNow().
7. 'Create item' in 'NCR History' for the decision, and Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email (V2)' to the raiser: subject concat('NCR ', Title, ': ', Outcome), body with the comments and the link.
8. Timeout path: a parallel case with 'Configure run after' set to 'has timed out' on the approval: set Status to 'Timed out', write a history row, send a mail to the quality manager group.

=== Error handling ===
Wrap steps 3 to 8 in Scope 'Try'; Scope 'Catch' (run after has failed or timed out) sets Status back to 'New', writes a history row 'Flow error', and mails the flow owner group the run link built from workflow() as in the other flows of this series. A rejected or timed-out NCR is a business result, not a flow failure, so keep those paths outside Catch. Do not use the 30 day maximum run time as a deadline: after 30 days pending steps time out (Power Automate limits page).

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
NCR-2026-0412, part 'Bracket, sample' (invented), Severity Major, proposed disposition Rework. Everyone-must-approve goes to the quality engineer and the production manager. Quality engineer approves with 'Rework per approved route'; production manager approves with 'Needs slot on Friday'. Outcome is Approve. DecisionSummary: 'Quality Engineer A: Rework per approved route | Production Manager B: Needs slot on Friday'. Status Approved, history gets three rows. If the production manager had answered Reject, Outcome would be Reject for the whole group, because everyone must approve.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Reading branch outputs directly. Skipped branches have no body; use coalesce as shown.
- Editing history rows. Make the history list append-only through permissions; versioning on the register alone does not show approvals.
- Putting disposition authority into expressions you cannot explain to an auditor. Keep the routing table in a list and read it, so changes are visible.
- Approvers who answer in Outlook and approvers who answer in Teams are the same record; do not build two paths.
- Case-sensitive compare. 'approve' does not equal 'Approve'.

=== Adapt it ===
Replace severity values, roles and the 2 day timeout. Add a column 'CustomerNotificationRequired' and a branch that only creates a task for a human to decide; the flow should not decide customer notification. For supplier-caused NCRs add a link to your supplier corrective action process.

=== Privacy and safety ===
NCRs name people (inspectors, operators) and sometimes customers. Restrict the lists to quality and the people who must see them. Comments typed into approvals are stored in Dataverse; tell approvers that the text can be audited. If you handle export-controlled or customer-restricted technical data, do not copy it into list columns or Teams posts. Keep it in the controlled system and link to it.

title: Power Automate flow: Part-145 shift handover reminder when no handover record exists
summary: Scheduled cloud flow that checks after each shift end whether every team has a handover record, reminds the team lead, escalates to the shift manager, and counts a 'nothing to report' entry as a record.
body:
Purpose: in maintenance organisations a good handover is a written record per aircraft or work order, not only a chat at the door. This flow does not write the handover for anyone. It checks that a record exists after each shift and chases the missing ones. A record with 'Nothing to report' counts, because silence is not information. The handover content and procedure belong in your MOE. According to a trade article (not an official source), Part-145 point 145.A.47(c) requires relevant information to be passed on at shift and task changes; check against the current regulation and your MOE before you cite it. Certifying staff decisions and release to service stay with people. This flow only helps with the paperwork.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'Teams and Shifts' (one row per team per shift: TeamName, ShiftCode, LeadEmail, ShiftManagerEmail). Use it as source so the flow has no hard coded names.
- SharePoint list 'Shift Handovers' with columns Title, TeamName, ShiftKey (text, example 2026-11-20-LATE), AircraftOrOrder (text), Content (multiple lines), NothingToReport (Yes/No), SubmittedBy (person). Your handover app or form writes here.
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.

=== Shift key convention ===
ShiftKey = shift start date + '-' + ShiftCode, for example 2026-11-20-LATE. Night shift 22:00 to 06:00 started on the day before the end, so the key uses the previous date when the flow runs at 06:15. Agree this once with the teams and write it into the form so nobody types it.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: 'Recurrence'. Frequency Day, Interval 1, Advanced options: Time zone your plant's Windows time zone (example 'W. Europe Standard Time'), At these hours 6, 14, 22 and At these minutes 15. Minimum recurrence interval is 60 seconds and runs are not guaranteed to start on the second, so allow a margin after shift end (Power Automate limits page).
1. Compose 'LocalNow': convertTimeZone(utcNow(), 'UTC', 'W. Europe Standard Time').
2. Compose 'Hour': int(formatDateTime(outputs('LocalNow'), 'HH')).
3. Compose 'ShiftCode': if(equals(outputs('Hour'), 6), 'NIGHT', if(equals(outputs('Hour'), 14), 'EARLY', 'LATE')).
4. Compose 'ShiftDate': if(equals(outputs('Hour'), 6), formatDateTime(addDays(outputs('LocalNow'), -1), 'yyyy-MM-dd'), formatDateTime(outputs('LocalNow'), 'yyyy-MM-dd')).
5. Compose 'ShiftKey': concat(outputs('ShiftDate'), '-', outputs('ShiftCode')).
6. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'Teams and Shifts', Filter Query: ShiftCode eq '@{outputs('ShiftCode')}'. Choice columns may need the /Value form depending on your column type; test in a run (check).
7. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'Shift Handovers', Filter Query: ShiftKey eq '@{outputs('ShiftKey')}'. Top Count: leave empty so you get all rows, and turn on pagination in the action settings if you expect more than the default page size (check the threshold in your connector settings).
8. Select 'TeamsWithRecord': From body('Get_handovers')?['value'], Map item()?['TeamName'].
9. Filter array 'MissingTeams': From body('Get_teams_and_shifts')?['value'], condition: not(contains(body('TeamsWithRecord'), item()?['TeamName'])).
10. Condition length(body('MissingTeams')) greater than 0. No: end quietly. Yes: Apply to each over body('MissingTeams'):
 a. Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email (V2)' to items('Apply_to_each')?['LeadEmail'], Importance High, subject concat('Handover missing: ', items('Apply_to_each')?['TeamName'], ' ', outputs('ShiftKey')), body with the link to the handover form.
 b. Delay 30 minutes, then repeat step 7 and 9 for this team (a child flow or a Compose of the same filter) and, if still missing, send a mail to ShiftManagerEmail.
Keep the delay short. A run that waits is allowed, but runs older than 30 days time out, and a delay inside Apply to each multiplies waiting runs.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' around steps 6 to 10 and Scope 'Catch' with a mail to the flow owner group. A failing reminder flow is itself a finding: the shift manager list must still be checked by a human at the end of the shift. Add a monthly count of reminders per team (Get items on a log list) to see where the process is weak, without ranking people.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Run at 14:15 on 2026-11-20 local. Hour is 14, ShiftCode EARLY, ShiftDate 2026-11-20, ShiftKey 2026-11-20-EARLY. 'Teams and Shifts' returns Line Team A, Line Team B, Base Team C for EARLY. 'Shift Handovers' has rows for Line Team A and for Base Team C (one with NothingToReport = Yes). MissingTeams contains only Line Team B. Its lead gets the mail at 14:15; if still nothing at 14:45, the shift manager is told. At 06:15 on 2026-11-21 the ShiftDate is 2026-11-20 and the code NIGHT, so the key matches records written for the night shift that started the evening before.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Running at the exact shift end. People are still writing; use a margin.
- Using the UTC date for the key. Around midnight the date is wrong for plants east of UTC.
- Counting only rows with content. A 'nothing to report' row must count.
- Matching on display names that people spell differently. Use a team code column.
- Daylight saving time. Check the schedule in the weeks when clocks change.

=== Adapt it ===
Change shift hours, add a fourth shift, or run per aircraft by reading an 'Active Work Orders' list instead of teams. Add a Teams post to the shift manager channel instead of mail.

=== Privacy and safety ===
Reminder logs measure behaviour of named leads. Agree with your works council what is stored and how long. Handover content can contain technical records and personal data; keep the list permissions tight. Copilot or flow text is never a handover and never a release statement.

title: Power Automate flow: weekly supplier certificate expiry reminder with 90, 60 and 30 day tiers
summary: Weekly cloud flow that reads a SharePoint supplier certificate register, groups certificates by days to expiry, mails owners and the quality inbox an HTML table, and marks expired entries for review.
body:
Purpose: supplier approvals, quality certificates and similar documents have an expiry date, and the date is usually noticed too late. This flow runs weekly, finds certificates that expire within 90 days or are already expired, sends one digest to the quality inbox and a personal mail to each owner for items at 30 days or less. It marks expired entries 'Expired - review' so a human can decide. Blocking a supplier in the ERP is a decision for purchasing and quality, not for a flow.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'Supplier Certificates': Title (supplier name), CertificateType (choice, for example Quality system, Special process approval, Insurance), CertificateNumber (text), ValidUntil (date only), QualityOwner (person), Status (choice: Active, Expired - review, Replaced), LastReminderTier (number, default 0). Store the PDF in a library and put the link in a hyperlink column.
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: 'Recurrence', weekly, Monday, 06:30, plant time zone.
1. Compose 'Today': formatDateTime(convertTimeZone(utcNow(), 'UTC', 'W. Europe Standard Time'), 'yyyy-MM-dd').
2. Compose 'Horizon': addDays(outputs('Today'), 90, 'yyyy-MM-dd').
3. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'Supplier Certificates', Filter Query: Status eq 'Active' and ValidUntil le '@{outputs('Horizon')}'. Order By: ValidUntil asc. Date comparison on a date-only column works with the yyyy-MM-dd text in most tenants; test with one known row (check).
4. Select 'Enriched': From body('Get_certificates')?['value'] and map an object:
 supplier: item()?['Title']
 type: item()?['CertificateType/Value']
 until: formatDateTime(item()?['ValidUntil'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')
 owner: item()?['QualityOwner/Email']
 id: item()?['ID']
 days: div(sub(ticks(formatDateTime(item()?['ValidUntil'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')), ticks(outputs('Today'))), 864000000000)
 tier: if(less(div(sub(ticks(formatDateTime(item()?['ValidUntil'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')), ticks(outputs('Today'))), 864000000000), 0), 4, if(lessOrEquals(div(sub(ticks(formatDateTime(item()?['ValidUntil'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')), ticks(outputs('Today'))), 864000000000), 30), 3, if(lessOrEquals(div(sub(ticks(formatDateTime(item()?['ValidUntil'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')), ticks(outputs('Today'))), 864000000000), 60), 2, 1)))
 One day is 864,000,000,000 ticks (100 ns units), so dividing the tick difference gives whole days. The long tier expression repeats the days calculation; in the designer you can instead use a Compose inside Apply to each, which is easier to read.
5. Create HTML table: From body('Enriched'), custom columns Supplier, Type, Valid until, Days left. Send one mail with Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email (V2)' to the quality inbox, Importance Normal, body with the table.
6. Filter array 'Due': From body('Enriched'), condition item()?['tier'] greater than 2 (tiers 3 and 4: 30 days or less, or expired).
7. Apply to each over body('Due'): condition item()?['tier'] greater than the stored LastReminderTier of that row (Get item by ID, or carry the number in the Select). If true: send a personal mail to item()?['owner'] (High importance), then 'Update item' with ID item()?['id']: LastReminderTier set to the tier; and for tier 4 also Status 'Expired - review'.
8. When a new certificate replaces an old one, someone sets Status 'Replaced' or creates a new row and a second small flow resets LastReminderTier. Decide who does that; flows cannot see a new PDF in a mailbox.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' around steps 3 to 7, Scope 'Catch' with run after failed or timed out, mail to the flow owner group with the run link. Leave 'Apply to each' concurrency off unless mails are independent; the limits page gives 1 as the default and allows values from 1 to 50 when you turn concurrency control on. Keep it at 1 here so the mail order stays predictable. If the list can pass 5,000 rows, keep the filter in the query so you never read the whole list.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Today is 2026-11-20. Supplier 'Special Process Shop A' (invented), Special process approval, ValidUntil 2026-12-18. Days: from Nov 20 to Dec 18 is 28 days, so tier 3. LastReminderTier is 0, so the owner gets a mail and LastReminderTier becomes 3. Next week the row is still tier 3 and nothing is sent again (3 is not greater than 3). 'Insurance cert B' with ValidUntil 2027-01-30 is 71 days away: tier 1, shown only in the digest. A row with ValidUntil 2026-11-10 is minus 10 days, tier 4: owner mail and Status 'Expired - review'.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Comparing a date-time with a date text. Normalise with formatDateTime before ticks.
- Sending the same reminder every week. The tier column prevents it; without it, people filter the mails out.
- No owner. Make QualityOwner required, otherwise item()?['QualityOwner/Email'] is empty and the mail action fails.
- Treating 'Expired - review' as 'supplier blocked'. It is a prompt for a human.
- Hiding the digest in one person's inbox. Use a shared mailbox.

=== Adapt it ===
Change the tiers (for example 120, 60, 14 days), add an 'Auditor sees' view, or send the digest to a Teams channel. Combine with an annual re-evaluation date per supplier by adding a second date column and a second filter.

=== Privacy and safety ===
The list holds company data, and QualityOwner holds names. Limit read access to purchasing and quality. Do not copy certificate PDFs into mails; link to the library. Retention of the register is a quality-system decision (check your procedure).

title: Power Automate flow: controlled document release with read-and-understood tracking per role
summary: Cloud flow that reacts to a released procedure revision in a SharePoint library, creates one acknowledgement per affected person, tracks the response with approvals and escalates open items to the line manager.
body:
Purpose: when a work instruction, procedure or checklist is released in a new revision, the people who work with it must know. Auditors in AS9100-style systems ask for evidence of revisions, release history and employee acknowledgement (trade sources, not the standard text). This flow turns 'we told them' into a record: one acknowledgement per person and revision, with date, and an escalation if nobody reacts. It does not release the document and it does not replace training. Release and training authority stay with your document owner and your procedures.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint library 'Controlled Documents' with columns DocNumber (text), Revision (text), ReleaseState (choice: Draft, In review, Released, Obsolete), DocGroup (choice: for example Machining, Assembly, Inspection), AckRevision (text, written only by the flow), DocOwner (person). Turn on versioning. Use content approval or your own review flow for the release itself.
- SharePoint list 'Role Matrix': Title, DocGroup (choice), Person (person), ManagerEmail (text). It says who must acknowledge which group.
- SharePoint list 'Acknowledgements': Title (DocNumber), Revision, Person (person), DueDate (date), Status (choice: Open, Done, Escalated), DoneAt (date and time).
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.
- Approvals run in Dataverse. Guests and users outside the environment are given the Approvals User role automatically, but assignment fails in some tenant settings (approvals documentation, read 20 Nov 2026); test with a real shop floor account.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: SharePoint 'When a file is created or modified (properties only)' on the library. Add a trigger condition in the trigger's Settings so the flow starts only for new releases:
@and(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/ReleaseState/Value'], 'Released'), not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/Revision'], triggerOutputs()?['body/AckRevision'])))
Column internal names can differ from display names (spaces become _x0020_); check the names in a test run. The condition also prevents the endless loop that would follow when the flow updates the file's properties itself.
1. SharePoint 'Update file properties' (operation PatchFileItem): set AckRevision to the current Revision value at once. That claims the revision so a second trigger does not start another run.
2. Compose 'Due': addDays(utcNow(), 14, 'yyyy-MM-dd').
3. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'Role Matrix', Filter Query: DocGroup eq '@{triggerOutputs()?['body/DocGroup/Value']}'. Choice values in filters may need exact label text (check).
4. Apply to each over body('Get_role_matrix')?['value'], concurrency 5:
 a. 'Create item' in 'Acknowledgements': Title DocNumber, Revision, Person, DueDate, Status Open.
 b. Approvals 'Start and wait for an approval' (StartAndWaitForAnApproval), Approval type 'Custom Responses - Wait for one response' with one response option 'Read and understood'. Assigned to items('Apply_to_each')?['Person/Email']. Title concat('Read ', DocNumber, ' revision ', Revision). Item link: the document link. Settings: timeout P14D. The exact field names for response options are dynamic; use the designer (check).
 c. Condition on the approval: body('Start_and_wait_for_an_approval')?['outcome'] equals 'Read and understood'. Yes: 'Update item' on the acknowledgement: Status Done, DoneAt utcNow(). A timeout does not reach the Condition, because an action that times out ends as 'has timed out' and later steps are skipped by default. Add a parallel branch after the approval with 'Configure run after' set to 'has timed out': 'Update item' Status Escalated and a mail to items('Apply_to_each')?['ManagerEmail'] listing the person, the document and the revision.
5. Mail the DocOwner a summary: Create HTML table from 'Get items' on 'Acknowledgements' filtered by DocNumber and Revision, sent when the Apply to each ends.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' for steps 3 to 5; Scope 'Catch' for failures with a mail to the flow owner group. Keep each approval at 14 days. Runs end after 30 days (limits page), so a longer deadline needs a separate daily reminder flow that reads 'Acknowledgements' instead of waiting inside one run. A person who is on leave: add a column 'Absent until' to the matrix and skip or re-send after the date.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Document 'WI-MACH-014' revision C is set to Released on 2026-11-20. DocGroup Machining; the matrix has 12 rows for Machining. AckRevision is empty, so the trigger condition is true; the flow writes C into AckRevision. DueDate is 2026-12-04. 12 acknowledgement rows and 12 approval requests appear. Eleven people answer within a week. One does not answer: after 14 days the approval times out, the row becomes Escalated, and the manager gets the mail. The owner summary shows 11 Done, 1 Escalated. When revision D is released, Revision D differs from AckRevision C and the flow starts again.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Starting on every modification. Without the trigger condition each metadata edit starts a run.
- Forgetting that old revisions are still open for people. Close or cancel old open acknowledgements when a new revision arrives.
- A single approval for the whole group. You then have only one response and no per person evidence.
- Using email replies as proof. They are hard to search and cannot be tied to a revision.
- Mixing release and acknowledgement. Do not let acknowledgement status release the document.

=== Adapt it ===
Replace groups, the 14 day window and the response text (for example 'Read, understood and trained'). Add a link to the training record. For safety-critical changes use a shorter window and a Teams message in addition to the approval.

=== Privacy and safety ===
Acknowledgement data is employee data. Agree with the works council what is recorded, who may see lists of named people and how long it is kept. Do not use the data for performance ranking. Keep the Role Matrix maintained by the line, because outdated matrices produce wrong audit evidence.

title: Power Automate flow: daily gauge calibration due check with reminder levels and overdue marking
summary: Daily cloud flow that reads a gauge and tool register, sends reminders at 30, 14 and 7 days, sets overdue items to a review status and summarises them for quality, with one reminder per level.
body:
Purpose: measuring equipment with an overdue calibration is a classic audit finding and a real quality risk. This flow reads the gauge register every day, sends reminders at defined levels, marks overdue items and sends quality a list. It does not decide about product that was measured with an overdue gauge. That is a quality decision under your calibration and nonconformance procedures. The flow only makes the dates visible early.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'Gauge Register': Title (asset ID), Description (text), Location (text), Owner (person), CalDue (date only), Status (choice: In service, Overdue - do not use, Out for calibration, Retired), LastReminderLevel (number, default 0).
- A second list 'Calibration Log' is helpful for an audit trail (one row per reminder or status change).
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.

=== Reminder levels ===
Level 1: 30 days or less to due date. Level 2: 14 days or less. Level 3: 7 days or less. Level 4: overdue. A level is sent only when it is higher than LastReminderLevel. This is more robust than 'send on day 30, 14 and 7 exactly': if the flow is off for a day (maintenance, throttling, failed run) nothing is missed.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: 'Recurrence', daily at 05:30 plant time, on Monday to Friday (Advanced options, On these days).
1. Compose 'Today': formatDateTime(convertTimeZone(utcNow(), 'UTC', 'W. Europe Standard Time'), 'yyyy-MM-dd').
2. Compose 'Horizon': addDays(outputs('Today'), 30, 'yyyy-MM-dd').
3. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'Gauge Register'. Filter Query: CalDue le '@{outputs('Horizon')}' and Status eq 'In service'. Pagination on, threshold sized for your register. Items already marked Overdue stay in the weekly summary, not in the daily reminder.
4. Apply to each over body('Get_items')?['value'] (concurrency 1):
 a. Compose 'Days': div(sub(ticks(formatDateTime(items('Apply_to_each')?['CalDue'], 'yyyy-MM-dd')), ticks(outputs('Today'))), 864000000000).
 b. Compose 'Level': if(less(outputs('Days'), 0), 4, if(lessOrEquals(outputs('Days'), 7), 3, if(lessOrEquals(outputs('Days'), 14), 2, 1))).
 c. Condition: greater(outputs('Level'), int(coalesce(items('Apply_to_each')?['LastReminderLevel'], 0))).
 d. If true: Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email (V2)' to items('Apply_to_each')?['Owner/Email'] with subject concat('Calibration due: ', items('Apply_to_each')?['Title'], ' (', outputs('Days'), ' days)') and Importance if(equals(outputs('Level'), 4), 'High', 'Normal'). Then 'Update item': LastReminderLevel set to outputs('Level'); if Level is 4 also Status 'Overdue - do not use'. Then 'Create item' in 'Calibration Log' with the level and the time.
5. For the quality summary, add a Select 'Enriched' before the loop (asset, owner, due date and days, calculated as in step 4a) and after the loop a Filter array 'OverdueNow' on that Select with less(item()?['days'], 0). If length(body('OverdueNow')) is greater than 0, mail quality a table (Create HTML table) with asset, owner, due date and location. A weekly second Get items with Status eq 'Overdue - do not use' lists the items that are still out of date.
6. When calibration is done, someone enters the new CalDue and sets Status back to 'In service'. A second tiny flow can set LastReminderLevel back to 0 when CalDue changes: trigger 'When an item or a file is modified', trigger condition equals on a changed due date through 'Get changes for an item or a file (properties only)' (GetItemChanges; the list needs versioning). Check the behaviour on a test row before you rely on it.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' around steps 3 to 5, Scope 'Catch' with a mail to quality and the flow owner, plus the run link. A silent failure is the worst case for a compliance flow, so also add a heartbeat: a weekly mail 'Calibration flow ran, N items checked' that quality expects. If it does not arrive, someone looks.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Today is 2026-11-20. Gauge 'MIC-0317' (invented micrometer), CalDue 2026-12-01, Status In service, LastReminderLevel 0. Days: 11 (Nov 20 to Dec 1). Level 2 (14 days or less, more than 7). 2 is greater than 0: owner gets a normal mail, LastReminderLevel becomes 2. On 2026-11-25 Days is 6, Level 3, a second mail. On 2026-12-02 Days is minus 1, Level 4: high importance mail, Status 'Overdue - do not use', quality list. Gauge 'GAU-0044' with CalDue 2027-02-10 is 82 days away and is not read at all by the filter.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Sending daily reminders. Owners then ignore all of them.
- Setting 'Overdue' only by color in a view. The status column must change, so filters and other flows can use it.
- Not resetting LastReminderLevel after calibration. The next cycle then never reminds at level 1 to 3.
- Putting calibration decisions into the flow, like releasing product. That is a human quality decision.
- A register that is not the truth. If gauges are missing from the list, the best flow is useless; do an inventory first.

=== Adapt it ===
Change the levels, run calendar days instead of weekdays, or send a Teams card to the owner. For equipment in a cleanroom or a customer-owned tool, add a column 'ResponsibleParty' and route differently.

=== Privacy and safety ===
Owner columns name people. Keep read access to quality, the owners and their leads. The register is a quality record; follow your retention procedure and do not delete rows to clean views.

title: Power Automate flow: Andon call escalation in Teams with timed levels and a closing record
summary: Cloud flow for an Andon call list: it posts an adaptive card to the team leader, waits for acknowledgement, escalates to the production manager and plant manager on timeouts, and records every step.
body:
Purpose: an Andon call says 'I need help here'. The flow supports the human chain: team leader first, then production manager, then plant manager if nobody reacts. It does not stop a line, a machine or a process, and it must never be the only way to raise a safety alarm. Safety stops use the physical stop and your emergency procedure. The flow is for the normal help call and for the record afterwards.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'Andon Calls': Title (area and station), Area (choice), CallType (choice: Quality, Material, Maintenance, Safety, Other), CalledAt (date and time), AckBy (text), AckAt (date and time), Level (number), Status (choice: Open, Acknowledged, Escalated, Closed), ClosedAt (date and time).
- SharePoint list 'Escalation Matrix': Area, Level1Email, Level2Email, Level3Email. Hard coded names in flows age badly.
- A way to create an item with one tap: a Power Apps button, a pinned Microsoft Lists form, or a Forms link on a station tablet.
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.
- The Teams actions that post cards need the Workflows app to be allowed in the Teams admin center (connector page). Check the 'Post adaptive card and wait for a response' action (operation PostCardAndWaitForResponse) with your tenant's real accounts.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: SharePoint 'When an item is created' on 'Andon Calls'.
1. 'Get items' on 'Escalation Matrix', Filter Query Area eq '@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Area/Value']}', Top Count 1. Compose 'L1', 'L2', 'L3' from first(body('Get_matrix')?['value'])?['Level1Email'] and so on. Use first() because Top Count still returns an array.
2. Level 1: Teams 'Post adaptive card and wait for a response'. Post as Flow bot, Post in Chat with Flow bot, recipient outputs('L1'). The card shows station, call type, time and two buttons, 'I am on my way' and 'Cannot come, escalate'. Use Action.Submit buttons in the card, which is the usual pattern for this action (Action.Execute is meant for bots; check what your tenant renders). Set the action timeout in Settings to PT5M (ISO 8601, five minutes; check that the Settings pane shows Timeout for this action).
3. Condition on the result: the dynamic output has the responder, the submitted data and the id or title of the pressed button (look at a test run, the keys depend on the card). Put a stable id in the data of each button and compare that, never the button title. If 'on my way': 'Update item' Status Acknowledged, AckBy responder name, AckAt utcNow(), Level 1; end. If no answer (the action ended with 'has timed out' in Configure run after) or the button 'escalate': 'Update item' Status Escalated, Level 2; continue.
4. Level 2: same card to outputs('L2') with the text 'Escalated after 5 minutes without answer', timeout PT10M. Same logic, Level 3 on failure.
5. Level 3: card to outputs('L3'), timeout PT15M. If again no answer, post a message in the production channel with 'Post message in a chat or channel': 'Andon call at [station] open for 30 minutes without acknowledgement' and mail the plant manager. Stop escalating; do not loop forever.
6. A second small flow or a button on the list closes the call. When Status becomes Closed, a trigger 'When an item or a file is modified' with trigger condition @and(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/Status/Value'], 'Closed'), empty(triggerOutputs()?['body/ClosedAt'])) writes ClosedAt and sends nothing. The second part of the condition stops the flow from triggering itself again after it writes ClosedAt.
7. The Andon list is your data for later: Pareto by CallType and Area, average time to acknowledge (AckAt minus CalledAt). Use ticks for the difference as in other flows of this series.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' for 2 to 5, Scope 'Catch' with 'has failed' only (timeouts are part of the logic). Catch sends a mail to all three levels with 'Andon automation failed, use the phone chain' and the item link. Keep a paper or phone chain as backup; Teams cards need a working connection, a logged in user and a phone with notifications.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Call at 10:12 local, Area Assembly, station 'Assembly 3', CallType Material. L1 is the team leader. Card at 10:12. Nobody reacts: at 10:17 the action times out, Status Escalated, Level 2, card to the production manager, timeout 10 minutes. He taps 'I am on my way' at 10:21. Status Acknowledged, AckBy and AckAt written; AckAt minus CalledAt is 9 minutes. The flow ends. If he had not answered, a card to the plant manager would follow at 10:27, and at 10:42 a channel message and mail.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Letting a flow handle safety calls. Do not.
- Waiting inside one run for hours. Runs time out after 30 days at the latest and every waiting run costs; keep levels short.
- Hard coded names. When the team leader changes, the flow calls the wrong person; use the matrix.
- Only testing with the flow owner's account. Test with a real station account and a real phone.
- Treating a card tap as a duty record. Acknowledged means 'seen and coming', not 'solved'.

=== Adapt it ===
Change timeouts, levels and call types, and add a branch for CallType Quality that also creates an NCR draft for the quality engineer to review. Teams message mentions are limited to 20 users and 20 tags per message (connector page).

=== Privacy and safety ===
The list records who answered how fast. Agree with the works council that the data is used for process improvement, not for individual performance ranking. Avoid free text names of operators in Title. Keep the Escalation Matrix editable by the production manager only.

title: Power Automate flow: daily SQDC KPI post to Teams from a SharePoint list with missing-entry check
summary: Weekday cloud flow that collects yesterday's safety, quality, delivery and cost entries per area from a SharePoint list, computes first pass yield and delivery rate, and posts an HTML table to a Teams channel.
body:
Purpose: an SQDC board (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) works because the numbers are there every morning. This flow reads the area leads' entries from a SharePoint list, computes two ratios, lists areas that did not enter data, and posts a table in the Teams channel before the morning meeting. It is a reminder and a display, not a measurement system. Define each KPI (what counts as a delivery, what counts as first pass) once, in writing, before you automate it.

=== Prerequisites ===
- SharePoint list 'SQDC Daily': Title (text), EntryDate (date only), Area (choice: Machining, Assembly, Paint, Final inspection), SafetyIncidents (number), NearMisses (number), UnitsProduced (number), UnitsFirstPass (number), OrdersPlanned (number), OrdersShipped (number), Comment (text).
- A Teams channel for the daily meeting.
- Licences and connectors: every connector used here (Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Planner, Microsoft Teams, Office 365 Outlook, Approvals) was shown as a standard connector when this entry was written, and Microsoft documents that standard connectors stay available to Microsoft 365 users (Power Automate licensing FAQ, read 20 Nov 2026). Always check the connector badge in the designer, your DLP policies and whether your environment is a managed environment, because those can change what is allowed.

=== Flow steps ===
Trigger: 'Recurrence', daily, Monday to Friday, 07:05 plant time.
1. Compose 'LocalNow': convertTimeZone(utcNow(), 'UTC', 'W. Europe Standard Time').
2. Compose 'ReportDate': if(equals(dayOfWeek(outputs('LocalNow')), 1), formatDateTime(addDays(outputs('LocalNow'), -3), 'yyyy-MM-dd'), formatDateTime(addDays(outputs('LocalNow'), -1), 'yyyy-MM-dd')). dayOfWeek returns 0 for Sunday, so 1 is Monday and the report then shows Friday. Public holidays are not handled; add a holiday list if needed.
3. SharePoint 'Get items' on 'SQDC Daily', Filter Query: EntryDate eq '@{outputs('ReportDate')}'. Date column filters can need an exact text form; test with a known date (check).
4. Compose 'Areas': createArray('Machining', 'Assembly', 'Paint', 'Final inspection'). Better, read them from a small list, so the flow does not change when areas change.
5. Select 'Present': From body('Get_items')?['value'], Map item()?['Area/Value'].
6. Filter array 'Missing': From outputs('Areas'), condition not(contains(body('Present'), item())).
7. Select 'Rows': From body('Get_items')?['value'], Map an object:
 Area: item()?['Area/Value']
 Incidents: item()?['SafetyIncidents']
 NearMisses: item()?['NearMisses']
 FPY: if(equals(item()?['UnitsProduced'], 0), 'n/a', concat(formatNumber(div(mul(float(item()?['UnitsFirstPass']), 100), float(item()?['UnitsProduced'])), '0.0'), ' %'))
 Delivery: if(equals(item()?['OrdersPlanned'], 0), 'n/a', concat(formatNumber(div(mul(float(item()?['OrdersShipped']), 100), float(item()?['OrdersPlanned'])), '0.0'), ' %'))
 The guard avoids a divide-by-zero error on days without production. First pass yield here is first pass units divided by units produced; your definition may include rework or scrap handling, so write it down.
8. Create HTML table: From body('Rows'), Columns Automatic.
9. Teams 'Post message in a chat or channel' (PostMessageToConversation): Post as Flow bot, Post in Channel. Message: heading 'SQDC [date]', the table, and a line 'No entry from: ' with join(body('Missing'), ', ') if length(body('Missing')) is greater than 0, otherwise 'All areas reported'. Teams message size is limited to about 28 KB including HTML (connector page). Check how the table renders in desktop and mobile Teams; if borders are missing, style the table or switch to an Adaptive Card.
10. Optional: for each missing area, send the area lead a mail with the link to the list form.

=== Error handling ===
Scope 'Try' around steps 3 to 9 and Scope 'Catch' (failed or timed out) mailing the flow owner group with the run link. If the list cannot be read, post 'KPI data not available, check the list' in the channel, so the meeting does not rely on yesterday's post. Do not post zeros for missing data: zero is a number, missing is a gap.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Monday 2026-11-23 07:05. ReportDate is Friday 2026-11-20. Rows: Machining produced 200, first pass 188, planned orders 24, shipped 21. FPY is 188 times 100 divided by 200, that is 94.0 percent. Delivery is 21 times 100 divided by 24, that is 87.5 percent. Assembly has an entry; Paint and Final inspection have none. Missing is the array of those two, and the post says 'No entry from: Paint, Final inspection'. A day with planned orders 0 shows n/a, not an error.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Dividing integers. Use float, otherwise some expression engines return whole numbers. Check with your numbers.
- Forgetting that Monday should show Friday.
- Posting values nobody validated. Add column validation in the list (non-negative numbers, first pass not greater than produced).
- Measuring people instead of the process. Show areas, not individual names.
- Adding KPIs until nobody reads the table. Four columns beat twelve.

=== Adapt it ===
Add a cost column (for example scrap cost, if your finance team defines it) or on-time delivery per customer. Link the table to a Power BI report for history; the Teams post stays the daily summary. For a long-term OEE view use a dataset in Power BI rather than extending this flow.

=== Privacy and safety ===
Safety incident counts can point to individuals in small teams. Post counts only, not names, and keep details in your safety system. Check with the works council that daily KPI posts per area are acceptable.
